haiku-low.q1: Captured amount minus the sum of pending and succeeded refunds; failed refunds are not counted. Checked under a row lock.
haiku-low.q2: It is retried up to 3 more times (4 attempts total) with the same idempotency key, 10s timeout each. If all fail, the refund stays pending.
haiku-low.q3: The refund is set to failed, the provider's message is saved as the failure message, and there is no retry. An audit entry is recorded.
haiku-low.q4: A refund moving to succeeded, either by a webhook commit (step 8) or by reconciliation (step 11). Pending or failed refunds never trigger email.
haiku-low.q5: The total of succeeded refunds decides it: below captured amount is Partially refunded, equal is Refunded. It changes only when a refund moves to succeeded.
haiku-low.q6: The transaction takes a row lock on the payment row, so other refund requests wait while the remaining amount is checked and the refund row is created.
haiku-low.q7: The refund's own id, generated when the refund row is created. It is stored as the refund's id, so retries reuse the same key.
haiku-low.q8: Signature is checked, processed event ids are ignored, and status changes only via a conditional pending-to-final update. Email uses a claim field set once.
haiku-low.q9: It stays pending, because the outcome is unknown and the provider may have created it. The hourly reconciliation job later resolves it.
haiku-low.q10: An hourly job asks the provider for each pending refund's status. Success or failure applies step 8 rules; no record marks it failed; still pending changes nothing; unreachable skips it.
haiku-low.q11: The refund shows as pending and is counted in the already-refunded total on the payment page. The document does not state any other message for this case.

sonnet.q1: remaining = captured amount minus the sum of pending and succeeded refunds (failed refunds not counted). The amount must be a whole number of cents, greater than zero, and no more than remaining.
sonnet.q2: The server retries up to 3 more times (4 attempts total, 10-second timeout each) with the same idempotency key, so no duplicate is created. If all attempts still fail, it goes to step 6 as an unknown outcome: the refund stays pending, the admin sees 'Provider has not confirmed yet.', and reconciliation (step 11) resolves it later.
sonnet.q3: No retry. The refund status is set to failed, the provider's message is saved in the failure message field, the admin sees the message on the payment page, and an audit entry records the status change.
sonnet.q4: A refund moving to succeeded: either step 8 (webhook) commits the move to succeeded, or step 11 (reconciliation) applies one. The email job is queued after the commit. No email for pending or failed refunds.
sonnet.q5: The sum of all succeeded refunds for the payment (pending not counted) compared to the captured amount: total 0 means no change, less than captured means 'Partially refunded', equal to captured means 'Refunded'. It is updated in step 9, in the same transaction as step 8, only when a refund moves to succeeded (not on failed or conflicting events).
sonnet.q6: In step 3 the server starts a transaction and takes a row lock on the payment row. Other refund requests for the same payment wait until the lock is released (when step 4 commits), so two admins cannot both pass the remaining-amount check.
sonnet.q7: The key is the refund's own id (the refund row id, created in step 4). It is stored on the refund row in the database (id is also the idempotency key), and the same key is sent on every retry attempt.
sonnet.q8: Webhooks: a processed event id returns 200 and is ignored. Step 8 uses a conditional update that applies only if the row is still pending, and succeeded/failed are final, so repeated or out-of-order events change nothing (a conflicting event is recorded in audit, event id still recorded). The webhook and reconciliation cannot both change the same refund. Email: the worker claims the send with a conditional update setting 'customer emailed' only if empty; if already set, nothing is sent.
sonnet.q9: The refund stays pending, because the outcome is unknown (the provider may or may not have processed it). The admin sees 'Provider has not confirmed yet.' and step 11 reconciliation resolves it later.
sonnet.q10: The reconciliation job (step 11), run hourly on a schedule. For every pending refund it asks the provider for status (by provider refund id if saved, else the refund's own id). Success or failure: apply step 8 rules (conditional update); on success, step 9 then step 10 run. Provider has no record: mark failed with message that the provider never received it. Still pending: no change. Provider unreachable: skip, status unchanged, check next run. It records last checked time and an audit entry per check.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED for a precise success view. The document only says the refund is created with status pending and that success from the provider means only accepted so status stays pending; it does not say what the admin sees right after a successful submission. (If the provider call times out or gets 5xx, the admin sees 'Provider has not confirmed yet.'; on a 4xx they see the provider's message.)
